## Why This Is Asked

Tests a practical, end-to-end multi-tenant onboarding flow in Azure DevOps, covering isolated namespaces, secret management, progressive delivery, policy enforcement, governance, and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for tenant onboarding

- Kyverno policy checks on manifests
- Approval gates and rollback/cleanup strategies

- script: |

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses end-to-end CI/CD workflows in a PR-driven environment with containerization, basic Kubernetes operations, and observability. Key emphases include reproducible builds, environment isolation, simple health checks, and resource cleanup to prevent leakage.

## Key Concepts
- Azure Pipelines YAML
- npm tasks (install, test, lint)
- Docker image building and pushing
- Azure Container Registry (ACR)
- Azure CLI for AKS cluster management
- kubectl for Kubernetes deployments and services
- Manual and automatic resource cleanup
- Azure Monitor logging integration

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  - main
pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndTest
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '18.x'
          - script: npm ci
            displayName: 'Install dependencies'
          - script: npm test
            displayName: 'Run unit tests'
          - script: npm run lint
            displayName: 'Run ESLint'
          - task: Docker@2
            inputs:
              command: buildAndPush
              repository: '$(ACR_LOGIN_SERVER)/app:$(Build.BuildId)'
              dockerfile: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/Dockerfile'
              containerRegistry: '$(ACR_SERVICE_CONNECTION)'

  - stage: Deploy
    dependsOn: Build
    condition: and(succeeded(), eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'))
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployToAKS
        environment: 'aks-pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: AzureCLI@2
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)'
                    scriptType: 'bash'
                    scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
                    inlineScript: |
                      PR_ID=$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)
                      NAMESPACE="pr-$PR_ID"
                      kubectl create namespace $NAMESPACE --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
                      kubectl set image deployment/app app=$(ACR_LOGIN_SERVER)/app:$(Build.BuildId) -n $NAMESPACE
                      kubectl expose deployment/app --type=LoadBalancer --port=80 --target-port=3000 -n $NAMESPACE
                      sleep 30
                      SERVICE_IP=$(kubectl get svc app -n $NAMESPACE -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}')
                      curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/health || exit 1
                - task: AzureMonitor@1
                  inputs:
                    alertResourceGroup: '$(RESOURCE_GROUP)'
                    metricsResourceID: '$(AZURE_MONITOR_RESOURCE_ID)'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests a realistic, beginner-friendly pipeline that covers core Azure DevOps tasks: CI, Docker, ACR, App Service slots, App Configuration integration, health-based swap, and Log Analytics auditing.

## Key Concepts

- YAML pipelines and multi-stage design
- Docker build/push to Azure Container Registry
- Azure App Service deployment slots (staging/production) and slot swap
- Azure App Configuration for per-environment flags
- Health checks and rollback strategies
- Logging/auditing to Azure Monitor / Log Analytics
- Service connections and least-privilege access

## Code Example

```yaml
trigger:
- main
pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest
variables:
  imageName: myapi
  registry: <ACR_NAME>.azurecr.io
stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: Test
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs: {version: '18.x'}
    - script: npm install
    - script: npm test
- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - job: Deploy
    steps:
    - task: Docker@2
      inputs:
        command: buildAndPush
        containerRegistry: '<registry-service-connection>'
        repository: '$(registry)/$(imageName)'
        Dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
        tags: |
          $(Build.BuildId)
    - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '<subscription-connection>'
        appName: '<app-service-name>'
        imageName: '$(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)'
        resourceGroup: '<rg>'
        slotName: 'staging'
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '<subscription-connection>'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        script: |
          HEALTH_URL=https://<app-service-name>-staging.azurewebsites.net/health
          if curl -sSf $HEALTH_URL | grep -q 'ok'; then
            az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app-service-name> --slot staging --target-slot production
          else
            az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app-service-name> --slot production --target-slot staging
            exit 1
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you add a retry policy for the health check without masking failures?
- How would you extend this to support a blue/green rollout for multiple regions?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Monorepo PR validation must balance speed with coverage by testing only affected packages while maintaining quality gates.

## Key Concepts
- Path-based triggers and changed files detection
- npm workspaces and selective package testing
- Dynamic matrix strategy and conditional job execution
- Per-package artifact publishing

## Code Example

```yaml
# azure-pipelines.yml
trigger:
  none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
    - '*'

variables:
  - name: changedPackages
    value: ''
  - name: workspaceRoot
    value: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)'

stages:
- stage: DetectChanges
  jobs:
  - job: GetChangedPackages
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '18.x'
    - script: |
        # Get changed files and extract package names
        changedFiles=$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD)
        packages=$(echo "$changedFiles" | grep -E '^packages/[^/]+/' | cut -d'/' -f2 | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
        echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=changedPackages;isOutput=true]$packages"
      name: detectChanges
    - script: |
        echo "Changed packages: $(detectChanges.changedPackages)"

- stage: TestAndBuild
  dependsOn: DetectChanges
  condition: ne(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['GetChangedPackages.detectChanges.changedPackages'], '')
  jobs:
  - job: TestPackages
    strategy:
      matrix:
        $[ each(package in split(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['GetChangedPackages.detectChanges.changedPackages'], ' ')) ]:
          ${{ package }}:
            packageName: ${{ package }}
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '18.x'
    - script: |
        # Install dependencies for the specific package
        npm ci --workspace=@myorg/$(packageName)
      displayName: 'Install package dependencies'
    - script: |
        # Run tests for the specific package
        npm test --workspace=@myorg/$(packageName)
      displayName: 'Run package tests'
    - script: |
        # Build the package
        npm run build --workspace=@myorg/$(packageName)
      displayName: 'Build package'
    - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1
      inputs:
        PathtoPublish: 'packages/$(packageName)/dist'
        ArtifactName: '$(packageName)-artifact'
      displayName: 'Publish package artifact'
      condition: succeeded()

- stage: QualityGate
  dependsOn: TestAndBuild
  jobs:
  - job: ValidateAllTests
    steps:
    - script: |
        echo "All changed packages have been tested and built successfully"
        echo "PR validation passed - ready for merge"
      displayName: 'Quality gate validation'
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle inter-package dependencies in the monorepo?
- What strategies would you use for caching npm dependencies to speed up builds?
- How would you implement test result reporting and coverage thresholds?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests PR validation knowledge, per-PR configuration management, secret handling in CI/CD pipelines, container image workflows, and security gates.

## Key Concepts
- PR validation with Azure Pipelines YAML
- Python 3.11 with dependency caching
- Azure Key Vault integration in pipelines
- Azure App Configuration for per-PR settings overrides
- Docker image build and push to ACR
- Health checks and merge gates
- Lightweight security scanning in CI

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
  paths:
    include:
      - src/**
      - tests/**
      - Dockerfile
      - azure-pipelines.yml

variables:
  pythonVersion: '3.11'
  dockerRegistryServiceConnection: 'acr-connection'
  imageName: 'fastapi-service'
  imageTag: '$(Build.BuildId)'

stages:
- stage: Validate
  displayName: 'Validate PR'
  jobs:
  - job: Test
    displayName: 'Run Tests'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: UsePythonVersion@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '$(pythonVersion)'

    - task: Cache@2
      inputs:
        key: 'pip | $(Agent.OS) | requirements.txt'
        path: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/.pip'
      displayName: 'Cache pip dependencies'

    - script: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt
      displayName: 'Install dependencies'

    - task: AzureKeyVault@2
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        KeyVaultName: 'kv-name'
        SecretsFilter: '*'
        RunAsPreJob: false

    - task: AzureAppConfiguration@1
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        AppConfigurationEndpoint: 'https://appconfig-name.azconfig.io'
        Label: 'pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)'
        KeyValueFilters: 'test-*'

    - script: |
        pytest tests/ -v --junitxml=$(Build.StagingDirectory)/test-results.xml
      displayName: 'Run unit tests'
      continueOnError: true

    - publish: $(Build.StagingDirectory)/test-results.xml
      artifact: test-results
      displayName: 'Publish test results'

- stage: BuildAndScan
  displayName: 'Build Image & Scan'
  dependsOn: Validate
  jobs:
  - job: Build
    displayName: 'Build & Push Docker Image'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: Docker@2
      displayName: 'Build and push image to ACR'
      inputs:
        containerRegistry: '$(dockerRegistryServiceConnection)'
        repository: '$(imageName)'
        tags: '$(imageTag)'
        command: 'buildAndPush'
        Dockerfile: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/Dockerfile'

  - job: HealthCheck
    displayName: 'Health Check Container'
    dependsOn: Build
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Deploy container for testing'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az container create \
            --resource-group rg-name \
            --name healthcheck-$(Build.BuildId) \
            --image $(dockerRegistryServiceConnection).azurecr.io/$(imageName):$(imageTag) \
            --cpu 1 --memory 1 \
            --ports 8000

          az container wait \
            --resource-group rg-name \
            --name healthcheck-$(Build.BuildId) \
            --condition Running

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Verify health endpoint'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          sleep 10
          curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Cleanup container'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az container delete \
            --resource-group rg-name \
            --name healthcheck-$(Build.BuildId) \
            --yes

  - job: SecurityScan
    displayName: 'Trivy Security Scan'
    dependsOn: Build
    steps:
    - task: Trivy@0
      inputs:
        scanType: 'fs'
        scanPath: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)'
        format: 'table'
        severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
        exitCode: '1'
```
